_doc: Gate map written by P1-GATES (BUILD_PLAN section 7, D-15); later lanes edit this file only as BUILD_PLAN section 3 D-15 lists, and a lane activates a gate by adding its marker file ci/active/<id>. A gate with cmd null runs the script ci/gates/<id>.sh (second-lane case files go under ci/gates/<id>/); defaultTimeoutS is the per-gate time limit in seconds and a gate's own timeoutS overrides it (ci/README.md). defaultTimeoutS is 300 s: the slowest gate measured green was unit-tests at 4.1 s (full --all run 7.7 s, 2026-10-31), so 300 s is about 70 times the slowest gate, leaves each of the two planned Playwright gates (expected well under 120 s) at least 2.5 times its time, and sits strictly below the 900 s checks job limit that also pays for install. 'when' is merge | wave | signoff | nightly | checkpoint (P3-CI-CADENCE, D-15; checkpoint is owner answer 24ad46b5, F-1410: a `when: checkpoint` gate runs only in `ci.sh --checkpoint`, the nightly set plus these gates, or by name with `ci.sh --gates <id>`, never in `ci.sh --nightly`; look-values-comparator-nightly is the one): a `when: nightly` gate runs only in `ci.sh --nightly` (or by name with `ci.sh --gates <id>`), never in the push set (`ci.sh --all`, the wave run); a gate with no 'when' stops ci.sh at start-up. 'activates' is the 1 task whose merge makes the marker owed (ci/README.md). Gates with their own timeoutS: by manager ruling (F-297, F-290), page-walkers 720 s (measured green 330 s in the wave run at 4b97bcb, .build/ci/wave-run-W13b.log) and import-target-counts with P2-SETUP among its builders, 600 s (D-15 as plan v0.11 amends it, F-314: measured green on the Spectre CI rig, the gate alone 3 times in the wave run's engine layout at ad4d078, 282.3 s, 260.6 s and 209.2 s; 600 s is about 2.1 times the slowest); and restore-test (D-15 as plan v0.11 amends it, F-387, F-400, F-485): 700 s, about 2.5 times its slowest measured green on the Spectre CI rig, 278.3 s in the wave run at dcb5ca7 (276.2 s alone at cd7aa37; .build/evidence/F485/). It replaces the 360 s that P3-BACKUP set from 117.5 s on a Mac rig before Spectre was measured. unit-tests and G-CI4 (D-15 measured-value rule, F-536, F-525: G-CI4 step 3 runs the root config 3 times): unit-tests 600 s, about 2.2 times its green 275.4 s on the Spectre CI rig in the push checks job's layout (the runner's pinned dind engine, cold, the job container on its own network), run sha 3761fc8; G-CI4 was 1260 s for the whole merge set until the P3-CI-CADENCE split (now 90 s, the last sentence and its note), about 2.1 times its green 602 s alone on Spectre in the same engine layout with the wave container's systemd pin and BW_WAVE_CONTAINER=1, run sha 3761fc8 (.build/evidence/P3-REPLAY-FIX/). F-410 (owner ruling ffd9f9ff): a gate with a parallel field runs beside other such gates, up to the run's cap (ci.sh --jobs=<n> or CI_MAX_PARALLEL; default 2 on the 8-CPU wave rig), never beside a gate that shares one of its parallel.exclusive groups (exclusiveGroups names each group and the resource it guards). A gate with no parallel field runs alone. F-485: a second group, heavy, keeps the long gates apart, and page-walkers has no parallel field, so it runs alone (exclusiveGroups). A lane that activates a gate adds the field only after checking that its script shares no fixed port, database, docker name, fixed path, browser profile, lock or log with another gate (an empty exclusive list), or names the group it shares (ci/README.md). P3-CI-CADENCE (D-15, Nov 2, 2026, F-575): the measured values, each from a Spectre run (.build/evidence/P3-CI-CADENCE/spectre/): G-CI4 90 s (28.1 s alone at baed10b, narrow-green; 23.5 s alone at 7dc3156, narrow-green2; 17.5 s in the push run at a7a17d1, push-wave) and page-walkers-nightly, set to 900 s then (547.6 s green alone at 7dc3156, narrow-green2); its timeoutS is now 1300 s because P4-ADMIN-IMPORT added step 5, from 885 s read on a local probe-only run at 809767e whose verdict was not kept, so 885 s is not a measured green of record (F-626); page-walkers is now 4350 s (F-1286: 2 x 2171.4 s, the page-walkers time measured green in 1 narrow Spectre run at run sha 08681a2b, verdict .build/evidence/NARROW-RUNS/ci-verdict-08681a2b3fa7-20261110-044116.json) and page-walkers-nightly 5300 s (F-917: measured alone on the Spectre rig in 1 narrow serial run at 994ff95e, page-walkers-nightly 3545.56 s with 2 cases red; page-walkers was 1449.39 s green there, a figure since replaced by the 4350 s sizing; see their notes). G-CI4-nightly 1000 s (461.9 s green alone at 1a39d60, narrow-nightly, F-576) is measured too. The one provisional value, with its trigger named in its gate note: look-values-comparator-nightly 900 s (84.5 s green at baed10b and 87.6 s at 7dc3156 in narrow runs; 900 s stays until the first nightly run on Spectre sets the value). F-1201 (manager ruling under the owner's CI cadence ruling of Nov 4, 2026, items 1 and 3; SPECIFICATIONS SD-38): a gate may name its runner, linux or mac; absent means linux. A runner mac gate needs this Mac (Xcode, the iOS simulator): ci.sh's merge, push, nightly and records sets never select it (only --gates by name), the whole-run cap of ci/wave-run.sh leaves it out, and the mac half of ci/wave-run.sh runs it on this Mac (ci/mac-half.ts, by the same when rule). native-no-demo and native-suite are the 2: native-suite (apps/tech-native/xcuitest/suite.sh) is when nightly, so it runs in the nightly and never in the merge set or the push run; its timeoutS 5400 s is about 2.05 times its measured green on the mac runner from a cold checkout (no ios/ and no build/, as in the main tree; F-1207): 2634 s in the nightly mac half at run sha 69df3377 (Nov 9, 2026: prebuild 29 s, cold build 189 s, then 6 classes, each on its own stack; .build/evidence/P6-XCUITEST-FX1/), the D-15 measured-value rule; a warm run, with ios/ current, was 2440 s (row 490).

exclusiveGroups.engine-net: F-410: the run engine's network namespace, where the wave container and every browser live (ci/wave-run.sh, --network container:<engine>). A Compose bring-up or teardown adds and removes interfaces there, and a Chromium page load in flight then fails with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED (F-290, measured: .build/evidence/F-290/wave-run-7ead420.log). So no gate that starts or removes a container runs beside a gate that drives a browser; these are also the memory-heavy gates (2 browsers, a 5-service stack, an image build), so they run 1 at a time. Membership is read from every file a gate runs, not only its script (F-464). Members: look-values-comparator (browsers), contract-gates, import-target-counts (ci/setup-stack.sh) and restore-test (their stacks), and map-manifest (infra/tests/maps-nginx.maps.test.ts starts and removes an nginx container), and unit-tests, kept in both groups by ruling F-525 (OA-88) and pinned by ci/run-gates.test.ts ('keeps unit-tests in engine-net and heavy'); no unit test starts a container today (the push-set tests use a fake docker, ci/engine-self-check.test.ts), so its membership is by that ruling, not by a mechanism, and the audit rule above (a gate that runs a file which matches the engine pattern) does not list it. page-walkers (browsers and 8 stacks, ci/gates/page-walkers.sh) needs the same, and more: it has no parallel field, so it runs alone (F-485).
exclusiveGroups.heavy: F-485: the wave rig itself (Spectre: Docker Desktop on WSL2, 8 vCPUs, 15.5 GiB, 1 virtual disk under the CI container, the run engine and its stacks). Two long gates side by side slow each other far past a fair share of 8 CPUs. In the wave run at d822332, page-walkers' shell-stack image build (pnpm install and next build on the run engine) took 335 s beside G-CI7's PostgreSQL step, against 32 to 88 s in the 24 other kept wave runs; G-CI7 took 287.9 s against 110.8 s (its CPU-only step 2: 30.2 s against 3.1 s). page-walkers and G-CI7 both hit their limits (.build/evidence/F485/). Members run 1 at a time: every engine-net gate (each builds an image, brings up a stack or drives a browser) and the 2 embedded-PostgreSQL gates measured over 100 s alone on the rig at cd7aa37, G-CI4 (216.4 s) and G-CI7 (118.7 s). F-915: and typecheck, CPU-bound (4 tsc processes at once, then the root tsc): 70.17 s alone at 1c6ea9cc, over its 300 s limit beside look-values-comparator-nightly at 806f63a8. F-1164: and G-CI2, 144.35 s alone at b405206c, killed at its 300 s limit beside look-values-comparator-nightly at 40f8433c. page-walkers, the longest (515.7 s alone, 72 percent of its limit), goes further: it has no parallel field and runs alone. Any other declared gate still runs beside a heavy one.
